mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the CPIAUCSL index (indicating elevated inflation) compresses real equity valuations through higher discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as inflation expectations become embedded in market pricing.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL is in the top 30% of historical levels (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering equity sell-offs due to reduced consumer spending and corporate profit visibility, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are positive in > 40% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp, or the Rank IC for UNRATE > 0.3pp change is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad consumer sector weakness, reducing corporate revenue visibility and triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through correlated demand destruction.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change < 0 and RSAFS monthly change < 0
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in > 40% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the interaction term (HOUST*RSAFS) has Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production contraction (INDPRO < 100) signals manufacturing sector weakness, reducing corporate earnings growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through supply chain and capital expenditure slowdowns.
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are positive in > 40% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC for INDPRO < 100 is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strengthening consumer confidence and economic expansion, boosting corporate earnings visibility and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through demand-led growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is in the top 30% of historical levels (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate increases above 4.0% signal aggressive monetary tightening, raising real borrowing costs and reducing equity valuation multiples, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through discount rate effects.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in > 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS > 4.0% is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE > 0.1pp monthly change) signal labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending power and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < 0 and UNRATE monthly change > 0.1pp
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are positive in > 40% of instances when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or the interaction term (PAYEMS*UNRATE) has Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth deceleration below 1.0% annualized (GDPC1) indicates economic slowdown, reducing corporate earnings growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through reduced aggregate demand.
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are positive in > 40% of instances when GDPC1 growth < 1.0%, or the Rank IC for GDPC1 growth < 1.0% is below 0.03.
